title: Alnwick Dolphins
text:
Welcome to the Alnwick Dolphins Volunteer Team!
Thank you for volunteering with Alnwick Dolphins.
Our swimming club cannot run without people who are willing to give their time, skills and energy to support swimmers.
Some volunteers will be visible on poolside. Others will work behind the scenes. Some will volunteer every week; others may help at occasional competitions or events.
Every contribution matters.
You do not need to be an experienced swimmer to volunteer.
You do not need to know all the rules.
You do not need to have volunteered before.
What matters is that you are willing to learn, work as part of a team and put the welfare and development of our swimmers at the centre of what you do.
This manual explains how volunteering at Alnwick Dolphins works and provides practical guidance for volunteers.
It should be read alongside the club’s formal policies and procedures.

text:
How do I sign up for a role, or find out more?
You can talk to your swimmer’s coach, or contact us at XXX. You will receive occasional emails from the club inviting you to sign up for sporadic volunteering opportunities - please do respond to these if you can!
When the club hosts its own events at Willowburn, its all hands on deck! There are lots of volunteering jobs needed to help an event run smoothly. Take a look at the Gala Roles section for some options. When home galas are added to Swim Manager, various Jobs will be available to sign up for via the portal - if you’re unsure, just speak to any member of the coaching squad or committee.

title: 19  Code of Conduct
text:
What does being a volunteer mean? Being a volunteer means more than simply giving up your time. When you volunteer for Alnwick Dolphins, you become part of the team representing the club. That means we ask all volunteers to: • act in the best interests of swimmers; • treat everyone with respect; • follow club policies and procedures; • maintain appropriate boundaries; • communicate appropriately; • work cooperatively with coaches and other volunteers; • respect confidentiality; • raise concerns through the appropriate channels; • provide a positive example to swimmers. You are not expected to know everything. You are expected to ask when you are unsure.
Our volunteer principles Everything we do as volunteers should support the club’s values. Passion We want swimmers to enjoy swimming and enjoy being part of Alnwick Dolphins. Belief We encourage swimmers to believe in themselves and their ability to improve. Dedication We recognise the commitment required from swimmers, coaches and volunteers. Respect We treat swimmers, parents, coaches, volunteers, officials and other clubs with respect. Teamwork Swimming may involve individual races, but a successful club is built by people working together.

title: Committee Roles
text:
These roles are held continuously from one AGM until the next. The minimum tenure is therefore one year, except in exceptional circumstances.
We always welcome enthusiastic new recruites, and if you have some time to spare we can work with you to help you find a way to contribute. However, these roles also benefit from some continuity, and are often held for a number of years at a time.
Where relevant, Swim England provides guides to each of these roles, which you can find on their website, and are linked in each role page that follows.

title: 1  Chairperson
text:
1.1 Requirements
The club chair is the principal officer for the club and is elected by the club members.
The chair provides direction and leadership to the club, dealing with issues as and when they arise. They are the ‘face’ of the committee and are intimately involved in all aspects of club organisation. This is a pivotal and highly rewarding role which success and impact on the club will be determined by your own ambitions and enthusiasms. As well as your ability to guide and engage others, it is an opportunity to take on a new challenge and influence the future direction of your club.

This varied role can (and does!) require a wide range of skills, including good knowledge of the club and competitive swimming, skills in organisation, diplomacy, public speaking and more. The time committment is varied but can be considerable. Its a challenging role but a massively reqarding one.

title: 11  Competition Secretary
text:
Alnwick Dolphins is a competitive amateur club. We attend a whole range of competitions across the region, and host our own fixtures at Willowburn pool. The competition secretary is responsible for maintaining the competition calendar.
The competition secretary gathers the relevant information, when available, for away events and adds them to Swim Manager, which is the platform that allows swimmers to enter events and pay their fees. This role is also responsible for communicating with the club to advertise upcoming events and to ensure everyone knows the opportunities that exist.
